To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the gross measurement of the tumors may underestimate 40 to 50% of their T‐stages in infiltrating lobular carcinomas of the breast, which may affect the prognosis.
the T‐staging of the lobular carcinoma of breast may be underestimated by gross measurements of tumors.
40–50 % of the infiltrating lobular carcinomas with gross size 5 cm and less change their T‐staging after extensive sampling.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the accuracy of the gross measurement of the tumor size in infiltrating lobular carcinomas and its effect on T‐staging, as well as the need to perform an adequate sampling of the tumor in these cases.
the accuracy of T‐staging in infiltrating lobular breast carcinomas.
the importance of microscopic restaging of the tumors of infiltrating lobular carcinomas, which are often underestimated by the gross measurements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a gross T0 tumor can be a T1, T1 can be a T2, and a T2 can be a T3 after microscopic restaging.
the gross measurements may underestimate the T‐staging of infiltrating lobular carcinomas of the breast.
T0, T2, T3, T4 tumors should be restaged after microscopic measurement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gross measurement of the tumors may be inaccurate and may underestimate the tumor sizes by as much as 40% in infiltrating lobular carcinomas.
a gross T0 tumor is a T1 tumor after microscopic measurement.
a T‐stage of 0 cm is not a valid stage for infiltrating lobular carcinomas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a more accurate staging of the tumor is required for a better prognosis and a more effective treatment.
a thorough sampling of the specimen is necessary to accurately assess the tumor T‐stage.
the T‐staging of lobular breast cancer should be based on the microscopic tumor measurements.
